comparator.name: Bachelor Biomedical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The September 2026 entrant curriculum follows Appendix 1 of the 2026–2027 regulations. It totals 180 EC, comprising a 150 EC major and a 30 EC minor. Year two includes three restricted elective choices worth 6, 6 and 5 EC. Year three includes a 22 EC integrated internship, individual thesis and oral defence. Article 5.3 sets progression and placement entry, and Articles 5.8–5.9 govern thesis and internship assessment. The 40 EC Dutch educational minor is a specific optional route.

core: How the healthy and diseased human body works, from anatomy and tissues to organ-system physiology
Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry and human genetics underlying life processes and disease
Disease mechanisms and pathology, the immune system, infection and inflammation, and finding better ways to prevent and treat disease
Pharmacology: the origin, molecular mechanisms, therapeutic use and toxicity of medicines
Human development and ageing across the life course, including the biology of age-related disease
Non-invasive biomedical imaging and visualisation methods; UCR computational image analysis is a partial contribution, not full acquisition or instrumentation training.

Biomedical research methods: designing and conducting biomedical experiments and laboratory techniques, statistics and biomedical data analysis, critical evaluation of published research, scientific writing and communication, and independent research culminating in a supervised thesis
adjacent: Biomedical science combined with general entrepreneurship, product-design, market and organisational perspectives; no guaranteed clinical translation, regulated product development or commercialisation training.
questions: Illustrative graduate research and career trajectories the programme prepares students for (cancer research, biotechnology, pharmaceutical research and development, health-policy work, public health campaigns, teaching biomedical science)

trace: Biological cells, molecules, gene variation, cellular physiology and research literature; genuine biomedical foundation.
Brain/neuron function, psychology and neuroscientific research methods; not full movement physiology.
Substantive cell structure, gene regulation, signalling, cell fate and drug-mechanism analysis.
Normal adult systemic physiology, homeostasis, metabolism, growth and ageing; explicitly not medical physiology.
Biomolecules, biochemical mechanisms and biotechnology foundations.
Introductory molecular/biochemical laboratory work, blood/ELISA, bacterial hygiene and GMO techniques; not the complete integrated placement or competence assessment.
Human pathology, cell injury, inflammation, genetics, testing/treatment and ethical context; not full reproduction/embryology training.
Epidemiology, risks, disease trends and evaluation of public-health evidence.
Functional anatomical systems, imaging/drawing/spatial reasoning and framed encounters with remains; academic, not clinical skills training.
Drug mechanisms, targets, pharmacokinetics, concentration/time responses and rational therapy.
Host-pathogen interaction, innate/adaptive immunity, inflammation and immunopathology.
Organ-system physiology/pathophysiology from embryology/anatomy to symptoms; not a standalone reproductive-development sequence.
Multivariate/regression/ANOVA/logistic and nonparametric models and reporting; stronger specific advanced-statistics relationship than general introductory methods.
Biopsychosocial psychopathology across lifespan; companion mental-health perspective.
Systematic reviews and meta-analysis using R across medicine and other fields; not an individual original biomedical placement/thesis.
Physical, cognitive, social and emotional development across lifespan, including prenatal/ageing; psychological perspective, not complete biological developmental disease curriculum.
Comparative/evolutionary neurobiology, biorhythms, animal models, anatomy, ethics and practical work.
General research design, sampling, statistics and group research; not full longitudinal biomedical competence assessment.
Data handling, cleaning, visualisation and own research project; no full machine-learning syllabus established.
Digital-image processing, features and segmentation with explicit medical imaging application; does not supply complete non-invasive acquisition/instrumentation training.
Moral theories, practical ethical argument, essays/presentations; not the complete Philosophy in Action trajectory.
Rhetorical analysis and academic written/oral argument; not full scientific communication/Endnote/MSF trajectory.
Venture ideation, design thinking, validation and planning; general enterprise foundation.
Financial statements and accounting; enterprise companion rather than biomedical discipline.
Consumer product design/development, prototypes, sustainability and basic IP context; no specifically biomedical regulated-product or clinical development project established.
Marketing theory, consumer behaviour, brands and responsible engagement; no biomedical-specific marketing training established.
Business strategy and digital transformation, rather than laboratory translation.
Customer/market research; not biomedical experimental or clinical research.
International business institutions, governance and corporate responsibility; organisational context.
Uses regression, classification, resampling and model validation on applied data, including examples from medicine.

alternatives.label: Biomedical mechanisms, health and research
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual sustained biomedical anchor and qualified companion perspective, without degree or professional equivalence.
alternatives.concept: Study health and disease through cell biology, anatomy, physiology, pathology, immunity and pharmacology. Neurobiology and lifespan development add perspectives on behaviour and mental health. Laboratory work, statistics, evidence synthesis, machine learning and image analysis provide complementary research tools.

alternatives.concept: Combine molecular biology, anatomy, physiology, disease mechanisms and biomedical laboratory work with venture development, consumer product design and market research. Accounting, marketing and organisational strategy help you assess how products and ventures are developed. These business courses cover general methods across industries.

alternatives.distinctness: 7 courses differ each way (52.5 EC). Venture development, product design and market research distinguish this option from the first option’s emphasis on neurobiology, lifespan development and evidence synthesis.

candidates.label: Biomedical Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Translational Science
candidates.assessment: Two qualified programmes retain the same11-course biomedical core82.5EC: foundations, cells, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory work, pathology/genetics, epidemiology, anatomy, infection/immunity, pharmacology and disease mechanisms. The primary adds neurobiology, developmental/abnormal psychology, systematic review/meta-analysis, quantitative/image/data and qualitative enquiry. These are genuine related contributions, not a reproduction of the Maastricht competency assessments or internship. The reconstructed enterprise direction replaces the former business-dominant proposal: it retains all11 biomedical courses including laboratory, anatomy, publichealth and disease mechanisms, plus22.5EC research/statistics/data and52.5EC enterprise/design/marketing/accounting/governance. Seven exclusivecourses52.5EC each way establish a real change in organising question, with sixadvanced courses in each. Business courses are taught as general business/design, not verified medical-device development, clinical translation, regulatory approval or drug-commercialisation projects. Source5585 supports an entrepreneurship profiling direction, not replacement of the defining biomedical core. Current22EC integrated internship/thesis/defence, scaffolded professional/communication assessments, advanced specialist depth and complete biomedical imaging/acquisition and machine-learning content remain gaps. Elective30EC is open subject to approval, not an assumed compulsory immunology package. A third biomedical-education candidate was genuinely reconsidered: UCR Rhetoric in Action includes didactic training and teaching children public speaking; other communication courses include literary stylistics, climate communication, creative poetry/performance and general persuasion. This does not establish a distinct sustained biomedical teaching/pedagogy curriculum. The official stable minor direction is education; general communication is a core competence, not by itself a separately established science-communication minor. Rejection is substantive, not merely absence of a teaching credential. No degree, professional qualification, master admission or career equivalence claimed.

candidates.label: Science Communication and Biomedical Education
candidates.assessment: Reconsidered actual seven MCCCOMM profiles. Rhetoric in Action teaches didactic methods and public speaking to primary-school pupils; no claim that UCR lacks all education practice. Other courses include Dutch language, literary style, climate communication, poetry/creative performance and general persuasion. These do not establish a sustained biomedical pedagogy/science-teaching programme. Official5586 supports an educational minor; science communication also occurs as a core competence, not independently established formal minor. A generic communication-heavy third direction would dilute rather than supply the missing teaching subject methods. No professional-license-only rejection.

blocks: Foundational life science: gateways, molecular and cell biology
Both study cells and the molecules that sustain them. Maastricht assesses this as part of its biomedical competency sequence.
Both study the brain and behaviour. Maastricht also addresses movement in the same unit.
UCR covers cell signalling within molecular cell biology. Maastricht offers Cell Signalling as one choice in this menu.
Human physiology, anatomy and organ-system function
Both examine how organs function and maintain homeostasis. UCR emphasises normal adult physiology.
Genetics, reproduction, development and ageing across the life course
Both address human genetics. Maastricht pairs it with reproduction and prenatal development.
Both address development and ageing. UCR approaches them through lifespan psychology.
Disease mechanisms, infection, immunity and pharmacology
Both examine how infection and the immune response affect health and disease.
Biomedical research methods, statistics, data analysis, laboratory technique and imaging
Both develop applied regression and analysis of group differences and repeated observations. UCR uses broader behavioural research examples.
Both develop laboratory skills. UCR covers molecular and biochemical techniques, while Maastricht assesses a separate set of laboratory competencies.
Both introduce statistical reasoning. UCR also covers general research design across fields.
UCR develops data preparation and visualisation. Maastricht combines data science and machine learning in a dedicated biomedical course.
UCR develops computational image analysis, including medical applications. Maastricht also studies how biomedical measurements are acquired.
Ethics, scientific communication and personal/professional development
Both involve ethical reasoning. UCR studies moral theories and their application across topics.
Both develop written and oral argument. Maastricht specifically assesses scientific communication and reference management.
Both include personal reflection and academic development. Maastricht links this work to its longitudinal biomedical competencies.

Additional disciplinary requirements and profiling space

notes.text: Maastricht assesses a 22 EC internship, thesis and defence, as well as dedicated research skills and a sequence of laboratory, communication and professional competencies. The UCR options provide related practice through individual courses. The first option adds machine learning and computational image analysis, while Maastricht teaches these subjects in a biomedical curriculum.
Maastricht’s 150 EC major includes three restricted choices in year two and leaves 30 EC for a minor. Optional UCR independent research is additional to each 180 EC plan.

audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Biomedical Sciences investigates health and disease from molecules and cells to organs and the whole human body. Students combine biological knowledge with laboratory work, data analysis, scientific communication and professional development. Restricted electives and a minor provide choice before an individual research internship and thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Both UCR options combine biomedical study with laboratory practice and research methods. The first adds neurobiology, lifespan development, machine learning and image analysis. The second adds venture development, product design and market research. Maastricht’s degree also includes dedicated biomedical assessments and a supervised 22 EC internship, thesis and defence.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC pathway includes three restricted choices in year two and a 30 EC minor. The 22 EC internship, individual thesis and defence have additional entry requirements.
